hints.quote: It's gonna cover the 8 major themes of the course.
hints.take: Learn the eight: anaphylaxis, hypoglycemia, asthma, chest pain, syncope, stroke, seizure and aspiration, each with its signs, first steps and drug.

hints.quote: you never want to be the one to stop the blood thinner
hints.take: The prescriber decides about stopping an anticoagulant or antiplatelet drug; you consult, use local hemostasis and document.
BLS is C-A-B: a 10-second breathing and pulse check, then compressions first.

hints.quote: That's probably one for the test
hints.take: Head tilt-chin lift opens the airway because lifting the mandible pulls the genioglossus and the tongue off the back of the throat.

hints.quote: do you put in the ankle? Do you put in the thigh?
hints.take: IM epinephrine goes into the thigh (anterolateral); know the site broadly, not to the inch.
Mallampati classes I to IV by what you see; III and IV predict a difficult airway.

hints.quote: a question that's going to show up on like every board exam
hints.take: Aspirated objects go to the right main bronchus: wider, shorter and more vertical.

hints.quote: don't do the blind finger sweep
hints.take: A blind sweep pushes the object deeper; remove only what you can see.

hints.quote: It's never wrong to call EMS early.
hints.take: EMS takes about 7 minutes or more; call as soon as an airway problem isn't resolving.

hints.quote: A common thing that shows up on exams
hints.take: Laryngospasm is more likely in a lightly sedated patient than in one deeply asleep.

hints.quote: Almost all bleeding can be stopped with gauze under pressure.
hints.take: Firm, direct pressure on folded gauze over the socket for 10–15 minutes comes before anything else.

hints.quote: What we want you guys to focus on really will be the management, and more importantly, the workup.
hints.take: Know who is at risk, which drugs matter and what you do in the office, more than the pathophysiology.

hints.quote: you are still the main provider
hints.take: A physician's opinion doesn't shift responsibility: follow the standard of care and document whom you spoke with.

hints.quote: I would rather deal with the bleeding
hints.take: Most patients stay on their anticoagulant or antiplatelet for simple extractions; you control bleeding locally.

hints.quote: Learn that number. Have it in your mind.
hints.take: Hypoglycemia (the lecture's number): serum glucose under about 50–60 mg/dL, with confusion, seizures and coma.

hints.quote: this is the information that you need to know
hints.take: Rule of twos: 20 mg of hydrocortisone (or equivalent) daily, for 2 weeks or more, within 2 years.
A nasal cannula runs 1–5 L/min (up to about 40%); for more oxygen, switch to a mask.

hints.quote: you're going to see this in your exams
hints.take: Severe local anesthetic toxicity is treated with IV lipid emulsion 20%.

hn-neck: Sympathetic = T1–L2 lateral horn; head fibers synapse in the superior cervical ganglion and ride the carotid arteries.
Parasympathetic head ganglia: ciliary (III), pterygopalatine and submandibular (VII), otic (IX).
Horner: partial ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis, flushing (Pancoast tumor).
CN XI is superficial in the posterior triangle: injury = drooped shoulder, weak shrug.
Great auricular (C2–C3) supplies skin over the angle of the mandible, not V3.
Hyoid C3, thyroid cartilage C4–C5, cricoid C6.
ECA: SALFOPSM; ICA has no branches in the neck.
Carotid sinus = baroreceptor, carotid body = chemoreceptor, both via IX.
Carotid sheath: carotid medial, IJV lateral, X behind; sympathetic trunk outside, behind.
Phrenic C3–5 on the anterior scalene; thoracic duct ends at the left venous angle.
Superior thyroid a. + external laryngeal n. (pitch); inferior thyroid a. + recurrent laryngeal n. (hoarseness).
Danger space (alar–prevertebral) runs to the diaphragm: route to the mediastinum.
hn-skull: Pterion = frontal, parietal, temporal, sphenoid; over the anterior branch of the MMA.
Epidural = MMA, lens-shaped, lucid interval; subdural = bridging veins, crescent; subarachnoid = berry aneurysm.
V1 superior orbital fissure, V2 rotundum, V3 ovale, MMA spinosum.
Jugular foramen: IX, X, XI, IJV; XII has its own canal.
Cavernous sinus: ICA and VI inside; III, IV, V1, V2 in the lateral wall; VI palsy first in thrombosis.
Petrosal sinuses drain the cavernous sinus (superior to transverse/sigmoid, inferior to IJV).
Anterior fontanelle closes about 18 months, posterior 2–3 months.
Tongue deviates toward a XII lesion; uvula away from an X lesion.
Stroke (UMN) spares the forehead; Bell palsy (LMN) does not.
CN III palsy: full ptosis, dilated pupil, down and out (PCom aneurysm).
Pituitary adenoma at the chiasm = bitemporal hemianopia.
Corneal reflex: V1 in, VII out; gag: IX in, X out.
hn-face: Blow-out fracture: floor most often; trapped inferior rectus (can't look up), numb cheek (infraorbital n.).
LR6 SO4, the rest III; SO is tested looking down and in.
Near vision: ciliary muscle contracts, zonules relax, lens rounds (III via ciliary ganglion).
Aqueous: ciliary processes → posterior → anterior chamber → trabecular meshwork → canal of Schlemm.
Facial nerve branches: temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, cervical.
VII closes the eye; III opens it.
Block too far back into the parotid = temporary facial palsy.
Danger triangle: angular vein → ophthalmic veins → cavernous sinus.
Scalp danger zone = loose connective tissue (emissary veins).
Tears: VII → greater petrosal → pterygopalatine ganglion → V2 → V1 → gland; drain to the inferior meatus.
Parotid: facial nerve (superficial), retromandibular vein, ECA (deep); duct opposite maxillary 2nd molar.
Parotid secretion: IX → lesser petrosal → otic ganglion → auriculotemporal; Frey = gustatory sweating.
hn-itf: Lateral pterygoid = only muscle of mastication that opens and protrudes; superior head to the disc.
Temporalis inserts on the coronoid; posterior fibers retract.
V3 lesion: jaw deviates toward the lesion on opening.
V3 anterior division is motor except the buccal nerve; posterior division is sensory except the nerve to the mylohyoid.
Chorda tympani leaves via the petrotympanic fissure and joins the lingual nerve.
IANB: pterygomandibular space (ramus lateral, medial pterygoid medial); sphenomandibular ligament to the lingula.
IANB misses the buccal nerve; too far back = facial palsy; medial pterygoid trauma = trismus.
PSA block too deep = pterygoid plexus hematoma.
Maxillary a.: 1st part MMA + inferior alveolar; 3rd part PSA, infraorbital, descending palatine, sphenopalatine.
Pterygoid plexus → cavernous sinus via emissary veins through the foramen ovale.
TMJ: fibrocartilage surfaces; hinge in the lower compartment, glide in the upper.
TMJ dislocation is anterior, in front of the articular eminence; TMJ pain refers to the ear (auriculotemporal).
hn-phx: Arch nerves: 1 V, 2 VII, 3 IX, 4 X (superior laryngeal), 6 X (recurrent laryngeal).
Arch 1: malleus, incus, chewing muscles, mylohyoid, anterior digastric, both tensors; arch 2: stapes, styloid, facial muscles, stapedius.
Pouch 3: inferior parathyroid + thymus; pouch 4: superior parathyroid + C cells.
Groove 1 = external acoustic meatus; membrane 1 = tympanic membrane; cervical sinus → lateral cervical cyst at the SCM.
Cleft lip: maxillary prominence + intermaxillary segment; cleft palate: palatine shelves.
Thyroglossal duct cyst: midline, rises with tongue protrusion.
Pharynx: all X except stylopharyngeus (IX); plexus on the middle constrictor.
Gag: IX in, X out; piriform recess fish bone hits the internal laryngeal nerve.
Posterior cricoarytenoid = only abductor; cricothyroid = external laryngeal (pitch).
Cricothyrotomy through the median cricothyroid ligament; cricoid = only complete ring.
Stapedius (VII) lost = hyperacusis; tensor tympani is V3.
Tegmen tympani roof: infection → middle cranial fossa; children's short flat auditory tube → otitis media.
hn-oral: PPF: rotundum (middle cranial fossa), pterygomaxillary fissure (ITF), inferior orbital fissure (orbit), sphenopalatine foramen (nose), palatine canals (palate).
Only parasympathetic fibers (greater petrosal) synapse in the pterygopalatine ganglion.
Sinuses drain to the middle meatus except sphenoid (sphenoethmoidal recess) and posterior ethmoid (superior meatus); nasolacrimal duct to the inferior meatus.
Maxillary sinus ostium is high on the medial wall; molar roots lie under its floor (oroantral communication).
Kiesselbach area = anterior nosebleeds; sphenopalatine a. = posterior nosebleeds.
Greater palatine n.: palate molars to canine; nasopalatine n.: behind the incisors (incisive foramen).
Soft palate all X except tensor veli palatini (V3); tongue all XII except palatoglossus (X).
Tongue: front 2/3 V3 + chorda tympani (VII); back 1/3 IX.
Filiform papillae have no taste buds; vallate papillae sit in front of the sulcus terminalis.
Submandibular gland: most resting saliva and most stones; duct opens at the sublingual caruncle.
Tongue tip and mandibular incisors → submental nodes; most teeth → submandibular nodes.
Apex above the mylohyoid line → sublingual space; below (2nd, 3rd molars) → submandibular space; bilateral = Ludwig angina.
da-numbering: FDI quadrants 1 UR, 2 UL, 3 LL, 4 LR (primary 5–8); #8 = 11, #19 = 36, #30 = 46, A = 55, M = 73
Universal primary: A = max right second molar, J = max left second molar, K = mand left second molar, T = mand right second molar
Succedaneous = incisors, canines, premolars; permanent molars are not
Primary order: central, lateral, first molar, canine, second molar (mandibular first); all in by about 2–2½ years
Permanent order: max 6-1-2-4-5-3-7-8, mand 6-1-2-3-4-5-7-8; max canine last anterior (impaction)
First succedaneous tooth: mandibular central incisor (6–7 years)
Primary teeth start calcifying in utero (4–6 months); permanent first molar at birth
Permanent root done 2–3 years after eruption; primary roots done by about 3 years
Primary: thin enamel, large pulps and high MB horns, cervical constriction and ridges, flared molar roots
Primary max central: wider than tall; primary max canine: mesial cusp ridge longer; primary mand first molar: transverse ridge MB to ML
Primary second molars resemble the permanent first molars of the same arch
da-anterior: Facial height of contour: cervical third on every tooth; lingual: cervical third anterior, middle third posterior
Overcontour: food skips the gingiva, plaque collects; undercontour: food packs into the sulcus
Distal contact more cervical than mesial, except mandibular central (level), mandibular PM1 and primary maxillary canine (mesial lower)
Lingual embrasures larger than facial; CEJ curve deepest on the mesial of the central incisors
Maxillary central: sharp MI angle, rounded DI; lateral: centered cingulum, lingual pit, palatogingival groove
Mandibular central: smallest tooth, symmetric, occludes with one tooth; lateral: distolingual twist, distal cingulum
Maxillary canine: longest tooth and root, labial and lingual ridges, mesial cusp ridge shorter
Mandibular canine: longest crown, distal ridge about 2× mesial, straight mesial outline, may have a bifid root
Centered cingulum: maxillary lateral, maxillary canine, mandibular central; slightly distal: maxillary central, mandibular lateral and canine
da-posterior: Maxillary PM1: two roots, mesial crown concavity, mesial marginal ridge groove, lingual cusp mesial of center
Mandibular PM1: canine-like, tiny lingual cusp, mesiolingual groove, mesial marginal ridge more cervical than distal (only posterior tooth)
Mandibular PM2: Y (three cusps, central pit) most common; two-cusp H more common than U; no mesial root depression
Maxillary M1 cusps: ML > MB > DB > DL, Carabelli on ML; oblique ridge DB to ML; wider lingually than buccally
Maxillary molar roots: palatal > MB > DB; MB2 makes 4 canals; mesial furcation most coronal, distal most apical
Mandibular M1: 5 cusps, 2 buccal grooves, D cusp smallest, ML tallest; M2: 4 cusps, + grooves
Mandibular molars: mesial root broader and curved with 2 canals; distal root straighter
Root trunks lengthen and roots converge from first to third molar; third molars most variable and most often missing
Centric cusps: maxillary lingual, mandibular buccal
da-anomalies: Gemination: normal count; fusion (dentin): one short; concrescence: cementum only
Mesiodens: most common supernumerary, between the maxillary centrals (diastema, blocked eruption)
Most often missing: third molars, then maxillary laterals and mandibular second premolars
Amelogenesis imperfecta: enamel only, normal pulps; dentinogenesis imperfecta: blue-gray, obliterated pulps; both hereditary, both dentitions
Turner tooth: one hypoplastic permanent tooth after infection or trauma to the primary tooth
Tetracycline: gray-brown dentin bands; fluorosis: mottled but caries-resistant
Dens in dente and talon cusp: maxillary lateral (anterior cingulum area); taurodontism: tall pulp chamber
Enamel pearl at a furcation: no attachment, localized pocket; dilaceration: bend of 90° or more
Erosion from vomiting: lingual of maxillary anteriors; abfraction: V-shaped cervical; abrasion: rounded
Tooth ID: class by cusps, arch by roots and tilt, then mesial landmark, then side
da-occlusion: Class I: maxillary M1 MB cusp over mandibular M1 buccal groove; maxillary canine between mandibular canine and PM1
Class II: mandible distal; div 1 proclined incisors + overjet; div 2 retroclined centrals + deep bite. Class III: mandible mesial
Centric cusps: maxillary lingual + mandibular buccal (1/3 in, hold VDO); non-centric 1/6 in, protect cheek and tongue
CR: condyles anterosuperior on thin avascular disc, teeth irrelevant; MIP: best fit of teeth; CO: contact at CR; ~90% slide ~1 mm
Optimal: even posterior contacts in CR, axial loads, immediate disclusion in excursions, posterior heavier when upright
Canine guidance: long roots, dense bone, fewer elevators fire; group function: canine + premolars (± MB of M1)
Nonworking contacts are the most damaging interference; balanced occlusion is for dentures
Taller cusps: steep eminence, deep overbite; shorter: overjet, acute Spee, plane ∥ condylar guidance, side shift
Greater intercondylar distance narrows the laterotrusive-mediotrusive angle (the only decrease)
Freeway space 2–4 mm; closest speaking space 1–2 mm; condylar guidance fixed, anterior guidance variable
da-tmj: TMJ: ginglymoarthrodial, compound; fibrous CT surfaces; disc center avascular and non-innervated, posterior band thickest
Superior retrodiscal lamina elastic (pulls the disc back); inferior lamina collagen (limits disc rotation)
Lower compartment = rotation; upper compartment = translation
TM ligament outer oblique limits rotational opening; inner horizontal limits posterior movement; stylomandibular limits protrusion
Moving right: right temporalis + masseter, left lateral + medial pterygoids
Rotation to 20–25 mm, maximum opening 40–60 mm; orbiting condyle goes forward, down and medial
Arcon = condyle on the lower member; facebow mounts the maxillary cast; protrusive record sets condylar inclination
CR mount can find MIP; MIP mount can't find CR
TMD: muscles most common; 5 factors; high crown → protective co-contraction; bruxism central; reversible care first
Occlusal trauma doesn't cause periodontitis or attachment loss; reversible; tooth 28 µm vs implant 2–3 µm
Miller 1 barely, 2 ≤1 mm, 3 >1 mm or depressible; abrasion: toothpaste matters more than the brush
f1-biomol: Noncovalent strength: ionic > hydrogen bond > van der Waals; hydrogen bonds need N, O or F.
Blood pH 7.35–7.45; a buffer works best at pH = pKa; bicarbonate is the main blood buffer.
Side-chain pKa: Asp 3.9, Glu 4.3, His 6.0 (the body-pH buffer), Cys 8.3, Lys 10.5, Arg 12.5.
Glycine is achiral; proteins use L amino acids; proline breaks α-helices (3.6 residues per turn).
Collagen: Gly-X-Y; type I is over 90% (bone, dentin, PDL); II cartilage, III reticular, IV basement membrane.
Vitamin C → prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase in the RER; no vitamin C = scurvy (bleeding gums, poor healing).
Outside the cell: procollagen peptidases cut propeptides; lysyl oxidase (copper) cross-links.
Osteogenesis imperfecta: type I collagen; fractures, blue sclerae, hearing loss, dentinogenesis imperfecta.
Hemoglobin: T (deoxy) to R (oxy), cooperative, sigmoidal; myoglobin: monomer, hyperbolic.
Right shift: ↑ H+, CO2, 2,3-BPG, temperature. Left shift: fetal Hb (α2γ2), CO, cold.
Glucose/galactose are C-4 epimers; glucose/mannose C-2; α/β are anomers. Sucrose feeds S. mutans glucans.
Triglyceride = glycerol + 3 fatty acids by ester bonds; A–T 2 hydrogen bonds, G–C 3; purines → uric acid.
f1-cells: Address tags: signal peptide → RER; mannose-6-phosphate → lysosome; ubiquitin → proteasome; NLS → nucleus.
Lysosome pH 4.5–5.0; peroxisome catalase breaks H2O2; mitochondria have their own (maternal) DNA.
Microtubules: spindle, cilia, flagella. Actin: microvilli, movement. Intermediate filaments: tensile strength.
Apoptosis = caspases, non-inflammatory; necrosis is inflammatory.
Reflection coefficient: 0 = freely permeable (no osmotic effect), 1 = impermeant (full effect).
Hypotonic → cell swells; hypertonic → cell shrinks. NaCl gives 2 osmoles per mole, glucose 1.
Na+/K+ ATPase: 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in (primary active). SGLT = cotransport; Na+/Ca2+ exchanger = countertransport.
Nernst: about 61 mV per tenfold gradient; resting potential (−70 mV) sits near E(K+) because of K+ leak.
Upstroke = voltage-gated Na+ in; repolarization = Na+ inactivation + K+ out; absolute refractory = Na+ inactivated.
Local anesthetics block Na+ channels from inside; acidic infected tissue weakens them. Tetrodotoxin blocks from outside.
EPSP: glutamate, Na+ in. IPSP: GABA or glycine, Cl− in. Ca2+ entry triggers transmitter release.
Botulinum blocks ACh release; myasthenia gravis = antibodies against the ACh receptor; cocaine and SSRIs block reuptake.
f1-molbio: Replication is semiconservative, in S phase; new DNA always grows 5′ → 3′ on a primer's 3′-OH.
Bacteria: primase → Pol III copies → Pol I removes primers → ligase seals; gyrase relieves supercoils.
Eukaryotes: many origins, Pol α/δ/ε, PCNA clamp; telomerase (reverse transcriptase) adds TTAGGG.
σ reads −35 TTGACA and −10 TATAAT; rifampin binds β; rho-dependent or hairpin + U-run termination.
Lac operon fully on only with lactose present and glucose absent (repressor off, CAP–cAMP on).
Pol I large rRNA, Pol II mRNA (α-amanitin), Pol III tRNA and 5S; TFIID's TBP binds the TATA box.
Cap (5′–5′), splicing (GU...AG, lariat), poly(A) tail (no template); acetylation on, CpG methylation off.
AUG start; UAA, UAG, UGA stop; wobble at codon base 3; peptidyl transferase is rRNA (a ribozyme).
AD every generation; AR skips (unaffected sib 2/3 carrier); XLR males via carrier mothers, no father-to-son.
Sickle cell = missense Glu → Val; frameshift = indel not a multiple of 3; Huntington = CAG repeat with anticipation.
Oncogenes one hit (HER2, RAS, BCR-ABL); tumor suppressors two hits (RB, p53, APC); HPV E6 → p53, E7 → RB.
f1-enzhorm: Endocrine = blood (GH, insulin); paracrine = neighbors (Leydig testosterone); autocrine = self (estradiol).
Peptides: preprohormone, granules, surface receptors, not oral. Steroids: cholesterol, carriers, nuclear receptors, oral.
Gs → adenylyl cyclase → cAMP → PKA (cAMP frees catalytic subunits); Gq → PLC → IP3 (Ca2+) + DAG (PKC).
Insulin: β cells, Ca2+-triggered release, receptor tyrosine kinase, GLUT4 to muscle and fat membranes.
Cholesterol → pregnenolone (mitochondria, P450, NADPH) is the rate-limiting steroid step.
Transcortin carries about 75% of cortisol; SHBG carries testosterone and estradiol.
Cushing = excess cortisol; Conn = excess aldosterone (HTN, low K+); Addison = low both, high ACTH, oral pigmentation.
PTH and calcitriol raise Ca2+; calcitonin lowers it (inhibits osteoclasts).
Catabolic: oxidative, exergonic, NAD+. Anabolic: reductive, endergonic, NADPH. Brain and RBCs: glucose.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; ΔG < 0 spontaneous, 0 at equilibrium; says nothing about rate. Enzymes don't change ΔG.
Km = [S] at ½Vmax (low Km = tight binding); kcat = Vmax/[E]; kcat/Km = efficiency (diffusion-limited).
Competitive: Km ↑, Vmax same (cross on y). Noncompetitive: Vmax ↓, Km same (cross on x). Uncompetitive: both ↓, parallel.
f1-carbmet: Glycolysis nets 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose; the rate-limiting enzyme is PFK-1 (on: AMP, fructose 2,6-bisphosphate; off: ATP, citrate).
Red cells end glycolysis at lactate (lactate dehydrogenase) to regenerate NAD+; the lactate goes to the liver (Cori cycle).
PDH works in the mitochondrial matrix with five coenzymes: thiamine pyrophosphate, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD, NAD+. It is irreversible, so acetyl-CoA can't make glucose.
Citric acid cycle per acetyl-CoA: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, 2 CO2. Rate-limiting: isocitrate dehydrogenase (off: ATP, NADH).
Protons pumped per electron pair: Complex I 4, II 0, III 4, IV 2. NADH ≈ 2.5 ATP, FADH2 ≈ 1.5 ATP.
About 32 ATP per glucose with the malate-aspartate shuttle, 30 with the glycerol 3-phosphate shuttle.
Cyanide, carbon monoxide and azide block Complex IV; rotenone Complex I; antimycin A Complex III; oligomycin ATP synthase.
Uncouplers (DNP, aspirin overdose, brown fat's thermogenin): oxygen use up, ATP down, heat out.
Glucagon and epinephrine → cAMP → phosphorylase on, glycogen synthase off; insulin reverses both.

Gluconeogenesis bypasses: pyruvate carboxylase (mitochondria, biotin, activated by acetyl-CoA) and PEP carboxykinase (GTP); fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase; glucose 6-phosphatase (liver and kidney, never muscle).
No net glucose from even-chain fatty acids or the ketogenic amino acids leucine and lysine.
f1-innate: Neutrophils are the most abundant blood leukocyte, arrive first in acute bacterial infection and make pus.
Mast cells live in tissue; basophils circulate. Eosinophils fight helminths with major basic protein.
NK cells are lymphoid by lineage, innate by function: they kill cells missing MHC I and IgG-coated cells (CD16, ADCC).
Primary lymphoid organs: bone marrow and thymus. Secondary: lymph nodes, spleen (filters blood), MALT (tonsils, Peyer's patches).
TLR4 senses LPS; NLR inflammasomes → caspase-1 → IL-1β and IL-18 (pyroptosis); RIG-I-like receptors sense viral RNA → type I interferon.
Respiratory burst: NADPH oxidase → superoxide → hydrogen peroxide → hypochlorite (myeloperoxidase). CGD: infections with catalase-positive organisms.
All complement pathways meet at C3. C3b opsonizes; C3a and C5a are anaphylatoxins; C5a draws neutrophils; C5b–C9 lyses.
C1 inhibitor deficiency = hereditary angioedema (low C4, bradykinin, swelling after dental work). C5–C9 deficiency = recurrent Neisseria.
Extravasation: selectins (rolling) → chemokines → integrin LFA-1 binds ICAM-1 (firm stop) → diapedesis → chemotaxis.
Apoptosis is silent; necrosis, pyroptosis and NETosis inflame.
IL-6 makes the liver produce CRP and the other acute phase proteins; IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α cause fever.
f1-adaptive: IgM: pentamer, first antibody, best complement activator. IgG: most abundant in serum, secondary response, crosses the placenta (FcRn).
Secretory IgA is a dimer with a J chain and secretory component (left from the poly-Ig receptor); it guards saliva, tears, milk and gut.
IgE sits on mast cells (allergy, helminths); IgD sits on naive B cells with IgM.
Heavy chains join V + D + J; light chains V + J only. RAG1 and RAG2 cut; TdT adds random nucleotides.
Class switching needs CD40–CD40L, cytokines and AID; a CD40L defect gives hyper-IgM syndrome.
MHC I: all nucleated cells, cytosolic peptides loaded in the ER after TAP, read by CD8. MHC II: APCs, engulfed peptides (invariant chain, CLIP, HLA-DM), read by CD4.
T-cell activation: signal 1 TCR with peptide–MHC, signal 2 B7–CD28, signal 3 IL-2. No signal 2 = anergy.
Th1 (IL-12) makes IFN-γ; Th2 (IL-4) makes IL-4, IL-5, IL-13; Th17 (TGF-β + IL-6) makes IL-17; Tregs need FoxP3; Tfh make IL-21.
Type I interferons from infected cells and plasmacytoid DCs make neighbors antiviral and activate NK cells, which kill "missing self".
Live attenuated vaccines (MMR, varicella, yellow fever) are not given to immunocompromised patients or in pregnancy.
Hepatitis B vaccine is recombinant surface antigen; anti-HBs of 10 mIU/mL or more after the series means protected.
Passive immunity is immediate and leaves no memory. Conjugate vaccines (Hib, pneumococcal) give T-cell help against polysaccharides.
f1-hyper: Positive selection (thymic cortex): weak binding of self-MHC survives, none means death by neglect; class I binders become CD8, class II binders CD4.
Negative selection (medulla, AIRE): strong binding of self → apoptosis or Treg. AIRE loss = APS-1 (candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, adrenal failure).
B cells: the pre-BCR uses a surrogate light chain; receptor editing swaps the light chain; mature naive B cells carry IgM and IgD.
Peripheral tolerance: anergy, Tregs (FoxP3, IL-10, TGF-β), activation-induced cell death (Fas–FasL). FOXP3 loss = IPEX.
HLA-B27: ankylosing spondylitis. HLA-DR4: rheumatoid arthritis. HLA-DQ2/DQ8: celiac disease.
Molecular mimicry: rheumatic fever. Epitope spreading: pemphigus vulgaris (desmoglein 3, then 1).
Type I: IgE on mast cells, minutes (anaphylaxis, latex protein allergy). Intramuscular epinephrine first.
Type II: antibody against cells or matrix (transfusion reaction, Rh disease, pemphigus, myasthenia gravis, Graves).
Type III: immune complexes (SLE, serum sickness, Arthus reaction at 4–8 hours).
Type IV: T cells, 24–72 hours (nickel, poison ivy, glove accelerators, tuberculin test, granulomas).
Penicillin can cause all four types.
f1-tissues: Hematoxylin (a basic dye) stains basophilic parts such as nuclei blue; eosin stains acidophilic parts such as cytoplasm and collagen pink; PAS stains carbohydrates magenta.
Ectoderm: epidermis, enamel, nervous system. Mesoderm: connective tissue, muscle, blood, kidneys. Endoderm: gut and airway lining, liver, thyroid.
Tight junction seals; adherens junction is an actin belt; desmosome is a keratin spot weld (pemphigus); hemidesmosome anchors to the basal lamina (pemphigoid); gap junction is a channel.
Epithelium is polarized and avascular and sits on a basement membrane (lamina densa = type IV collagen).
Simple squamous: alveoli, vessels. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar: airways. Transitional: bladder.
Attached gingiva and hard palate: keratinized or parakeratinized stratified squamous; cheek and floor of mouth: nonkeratinized.
Microvilli: actin core, still. Cilia: 9+2 microtubules, dynein, they beat.
Merocrine (salivary glands), apocrine (mammary lipid), holocrine (sebaceous glands).
Collagen I: bone, dentin, tendon; II: cartilage; III: reticular fibers; IV: basal lamina. Vitamin C is needed (scurvy).
Serum is plasma without clotting factors. White fat is unilocular; brown fat is multilocular and makes heat with thermogenin.
f2-genpath: First sign of reversible injury: cell swelling (sodium pump fails)
Coagulative = infarct outside the brain; liquefactive = brain and abscess; caseous = TB; fat = pancreatitis
Apoptosis: no inflammation; intrinsic = cytochrome c, extrinsic = FasL binds Fas; both end in caspases
Free radical scavengers: superoxide dismutase, catalase, glutathione peroxidase
Metaplasia: columnar to squamous in a smoker's bronchus
Dystrophic calcification: normal calcium, damaged tissue; metastatic: high calcium, normal tissue
M1 = IFN-γ, kill; M2 = IL-4 and IL-13, heal with IL-10 and TGF-β
Keloid grows past the wound edge and doesn't regress; hypertrophic scar stays inside
Hepcidin = anemia of chronic disease; CRP = opsonin and cardiac risk marker
Stage (TNM) predicts prognosis better than grade (differentiation)
f2-virology: Naked viruses survive drying and the gut (HAV, HEV, HPV, polio); enveloped ones need to stay wet

Principles = aspirational; Code of Professional Conduct = binding on members; advisory opinions = the Council's interpretations.

Records (1.B): copies to the patient or new dentist, free or at nominal cost, paid or not; sensitive information needs written permission.
Impaired colleague (2.D): urge treatment; with first-hand knowledge, report to the dental society's professional assistance committee.
Postexposure (2.E): tell the exposed patient and refer; if you're the source, share your status and get tested.
Abandonment (2.F): adequate notice and time to find another dentist.
Abuse (3.E): report suspected cases as state law requires; respect a competent adult's wish when no report is mandated.
Patient selection (4.A): no refusal for race, creed, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or disability, including HIV.
Emergency (4.B): arrange care even for patients not of record, then return them to their dentist.
Justifiable criticism (4.C): no disparaging remarks; report gross or continual faulty treatment.
No detox amalgam removal (5.A.1), no undisclosed copay waivers (5.B.1), no higher fee for the insured (5.B.2), no split fees (4.E).

Canterbury v. Spence (1972): the reasonable-patient standard of disclosure.
Capacity: understand, appreciate, reason, express a choice; competence is a court's finding.
Informed refusal: explain, document, sign; a patient can't demand care below the standard.
Minors: a parent or legal guardian consents (the custodial parent after a divorce); emancipated minors consent for themselves.
HIPAA: PHI in any form; no authorization needed for treatment, payment, operations or legally required reports.
Minimum necessary doesn't apply to sharing for treatment; patients get copies within 30 days.
Tarasoff: a duty to protect an identifiable person from a patient's serious threat.
Child abuse: report a reasonable suspicion; no proof needed; good-faith reporters are immune.
Needlestick risk: HBV about 30%, HCV about 2%, HIV about 0.3%; only HBV has a vaccine, offered free.
After an exposure: wash, report, HIV prophylaxis ideally within 2 hours and by 72.
Valid = the structure guarantees the conclusion; sound = valid with true premises.
eb-ask: The 5 A's: ask, acquire, appraise, apply, assess, always in that order.
PICO(T): patient or problem, intervention, comparison, outcome, time; only foreground (comparison) questions fit PICO.
Search TRIP first, then PubMed Clinical Queries, then the Cochrane Library.
Starts with the disease and looks back = case-control (odds ratio); starts with the exposure and follows forward = cohort (incidence, relative risk).
Case-control suits rare diseases; cohort suits rare exposures.
Cross-sectional = one snapshot, prevalence; ecological = group averages, prone to the ecological fallacy.
The RCT is the only true experiment and the best single study for a therapy question.
Pyramid, bottom to top: lab and animal → case reports and expert opinion → ecological → cross-sectional → case-control → cohort → RCT → systematic review and meta-analysis → guideline.
Meta-analysis = systematic review + pooled summary statistic; a literature review has no method.
GRADE rates the certainty of evidence (high to very low); AGREE appraises guidelines; CONSORT reports RCTs, STROBE observational studies.
Efficacy = ideal conditions (academic RCT); effectiveness = everyday practice.
Knowledge gap → efficacy and effectiveness studies; knowing gap → dissemination; knowing-to-doing gap → implementation.
eb-appraise: Internal validity = believable for the subjects; external validity = applies to your patients.
Bias = systematic error; confounding = a third factor tied to exposure and outcome; chance = random sampling variation.
Randomization balances known and unknown confounders; blinding prevents measurement bias.
Intention-to-treat = analyze everyone as randomized; per-protocol = only those who completed.
Precision = repeatable; accuracy = true. Standardization = same rules; calibration = scores agree.
Incidence = new cases over time (cohort); prevalence = existing cases now (cross-sectional).
Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN), SnNout, for screening; specificity = TN/(TN+FP), SpPin, for confirming.
As prevalence falls, PPV falls and NPV rises; sensitivity and specificity don't change.
A ratio of 1 = no difference, above 1 = harmful, below 1 = protective; a CI that includes 1 = not significant.
NNT = 1/ARR, rounded up; lower is better.
Type I = false positive (alpha, 0.05); type II = false negative (beta); power = 1 − beta.
The median beats the mean for skewed data; statistical significance isn't clinical importance.
rd-physics: Cathode (−) makes electrons; anode (+) tungsten target; >99% heat, ~1% x-rays.
Bremsstrahlung = primary source (continuous spectrum); characteristic = minor.
mA and time = photon quantity; kVp = energy/penetration (beam quality).
Inverse square law: double the distance → 1/4 the intensity.
Filtration removes low-energy photons; collimation restricts beam, cuts scatter and dose.
Compton ~57% (fog, lowers contrast); photoelectric ~27% (makes the image, ∝ Z³, bone 6.5×); coherent ~7%.
~9% of photons pass through without interacting.
Small focal spot = sharper image + more heat.
High contrast = short grayscale (low kVp); low contrast = long grayscale (high kVp).
Intraoral settings ≈ 7–10 mA, 65–70 kVp; sharpness is lost to motion.

Deterministic: threshold, severity rises with dose (xerostomia, ORN, cataracts).
Stochastic: no threshold, probability rises with dose (cancer, heritable).
Children ~3× adult tumor risk; dental doses can't harm a fetus.
ALARA = As Low As Reasonably Achievable; ALADA = as diagnostically achievable.
Three principles: justification, optimization (ALARA), dose limitation (staff, not patients).
Rectangular collimation ~60% less area; thyroid collar; fast receptors.

Low sharpness is never diagnostic — retake.

Normal rate 60–100; AFib: clots and stroke risk, so anticoagulated.
Prophylaxis: prosthetic valve or material, past IE, unrepaired cyanotic CHD, repaired CHD with prosthetic material, transplant with valvulopathy.

Syncope: fear or pain, prodrome (pale, sweaty, lightheaded), slow pulse; legs up, quick recovery.
Diabetes: fasting 126, random 200, HbA1c 6.5%; HbA1c over 10 poor control.
Hypoglycemia (lecture): under about 50–60 mg/dL; low sugar is worse than high.
Conscious: juice or gel. Unconscious: glucagon 1 mg IM or 50 mL of 50% dextrose IV.
1 g of sugar raises glucose about 3–5 mg/dL; glucagon reaches about 130 in 25–30 min.
Nasal cannula 1–5 L/min, up to about 40%; face mask up to about 60%; non-rebreather 15 L the highest.

Adrenal crisis: hypotension, vomiting, confusion; hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM.
Thyroid storm: fever, racing heart, agitation after infection or surgery; stop and transport.
Seizure: protect, don't restrain, nothing in the mouth; long one: benzodiazepine and 911.
Lidocaine 2% with epi: 36 mg per cartridge, 7 mg/kg, about 13 for 70 kg; severe toxicity: IV lipid emulsion 20%.
